Medicaid has come a long way in 60 years, from covering the most vulnerable to becoming a cornerstone of our health system. Now, it faces serious challenges. I am honored to join @SenatorATW  and Delegates Ashanti Martinez and Nicole Williams in Greenbelt on Wednesday, July 30, 10 AM–12 PM for a town hall meeting celebrating this milestone and discussing the consequences of the One Big Ugly Bill.  

🗣Please bring your questions, stories, and ideas. We want this to be a conversation, not just a briefing.  

RSVP using: https://t.co/cirwz17RKO

📣 Friendly Reminder: Just 2 Days Until Our Medicaid Town Hall in Greenbelt!

Join us Wednesday, July 30, from 10 AM to 12 PM, as I sit down with @SenatorATW, Delegates Ashanti Martinez and Nicole Williams in Greenbelt to celebrate Medicaid’s 60-year legacy—and dig into what this legislation really means for our community.

Your voice matters: bring your questions, stories, feedback. We want a real conversation—not just a briefing.

🎟️ RSVP here: https://t.co/cirwz17jVg

Together, let's ensure Medicaid continues to serve people—not get sacrificed for tax breaks benefiting the wealthy.

As we celebrate this 60-year milestone of Medicare and Medicaid, let's renew our promise: Medicare and Medicaid are not relics of the past—they are essential lifelines we rely on today.

I remain dedicated to protecting and strengthening access to affordable healthcare for every American—no matter your age or income.

Today’s Medicare Town Hall was more than a policy discussion—it was a wake-up call.

We heard from Sheila Lemus, a constituent living with MS, who survived thanks to Medicaid. But under H.R. 1, folks like Sheila—along with working families, seniors, disabled Americans, and kids with special needs—are being left behind.

This bill guts care when we should be expanding it.

We hosted this dialogue to shine a light on the real consequences of these reckless cuts—and to recommit ourselves to the fight for affordable, accessible health care in Maryland and across the country. 🩺✊🏽

#ProtectMedicare #MedicaidMatters #MD04

We are working with our state and local partners to counteract these Medicare Cuts on the 60th Anniversary of this life saving program.  We held a town hall in Greenbelt, Maryland with Delegate Ashanti Martinez and healthcare providers to discuss:
H.R. 1, Republican's Big Ugly Bill:
• 331,000 Marylanders will be affected by cuts to Medicaid
• 175,000 Marylanders will lose health care
• 60,000 legal migrants in Maryland will lose health care
• 350 DACA recipients will lose health care
• The state of Maryland will lose $2.7 billion in federal funding annually.

The Trump Administration’s reckless plan to shut down the Beltsville Agricultural Research Center is unacceptable. 

For more than a century, BARC has been a global leader in food safety, human health, and nutrition. Closing it would devastate Maryland, undermine American agriculture, and waste generations of expertise.

I stand firmly with my Maryland Delegation colleagues, local scientists, and community leaders in fighting to keep BARC open. We will not allow political games to dismantle an institution so vital to our farmers, our food supply, and our future.

https://t.co/9iTNHfohu6

Republicans are waging the biggest attack on healthcare in our nation’s history. In Maryland alone, over 247,000 people with ACA coverage will see their premiums jump by an average of 17% if subsidies expire.
At a time when costs are already crushing households, this is unacceptable. 

Republicans in Congress must extend these life-saving tax credits now—or own the healthcare crisis they’re creating.

The Republicans refused to work with us on a bipartisan funding bill that would keep the government open and protect healthcare. American families are feeling the economic pinch. 

We need solutions to address our problems not more of the same nonsense.
